§. 3. Consequens horum molimimum notatur, fore ut
ipsis sit in direptiones, & in rapinam. Ita notatur
successus opponentium in certo tempore, משׂסות [?] sunt
direptiones, quales à deviétis hostibus fieri solent, quando
milites victores hostium debellatorum & fugatorum
castra rapiunt, & quisque prædæ partem aufert. Hoc
sensu verbum שׁסה [?] occurrit 1 Sam. 17:53. Cons.
Jud. 2:14. Hinc & nomen, ab hoc verbo derivatum, pro
direptione venit, 2 Reg. 21:14. Jes. 42:22. 24.
Neque omittendum, quod vox in plurali hic notet amplissimam
direptionem, plusquam in uno loco ferendam,
& plus quam unâ vice subeundam. Cederent

page.notes: The Hebrew words are printed in Hebrew letters; the pointing and the exact letters of the first word (משׂסות) and the verb root (שׁסה) are uncertain. The Roman-letter catchword is the second half of "articulus". The long s in "Confequens", "Conf." and "Jef." is read as plain s, as instructed. A dot below the text is not printed text.
